def: Training a pretrained model on example prompt and response pairs with the next-token loss, counting only the response tokens. Teaches format and behaviour more than knowledge.

The claim from LIMA (Zhou et al., 2023) that a model's knowledge comes almost entirely from pretraining and alignment mostly teaches which format and style to use. Holds for style, less so for hard skills.
The exact layout of special tokens and role markers used to format a conversation. Training, serving, and evaluation must all use the same one.
Setting the label of non-target tokens (system, user, tool output) to an ignore value such as -100 so they don't contribute to the loss.
Training each step on the reference's previous tokens rather than the model's own. Causes exposure bias, because at inference the model conditions on its own outputs.
Concatenating several short training examples into one fixed-length sequence to avoid wasted padding. Needs per-document attention masks so examples can't see each other.
Loss of previously learned abilities when a model is trained further on narrow data. Detected with a fixed regression suite compared against the parent model.
Mixing general or earlier training data into a narrow fine-tuning run to reduce forgetting.
Methods that freeze the pretrained weights and train a small number of added or selected parameters.
Low-Rank Adaptation (Hu et al., 2021). Learns a low-rank update BA added to a frozen weight, scaled by alpha/r. B starts at zero so training begins at the base model.
The inner dimension r of the LoRA matrices. The update can express at most r independent directions; trainable parameters per matrix are r times (rows + columns).
LoRA trained on top of a base model stored in 4-bit NF4, with double quantisation and paged optimisers (Dettmers et al., 2023). Cuts memory enough to fine-tune large models on one GPU.
4-bit NormalFloat: a 4-bit data type whose levels sit at quantiles of a normal distribution, suited to normally distributed weights.
Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (Liu et al., 2024). Splits each weight into magnitude and direction and applies LoRA to the direction.
The number of free directions needed to reach most of full fine-tuning performance. Low for pretrained language models, which is why low-rank updates work.
Folding a trained LoRA update into the base weights (W + (alpha/r)BA) so serving has no extra cost. Inexact when the base is quantised.
Serving many adapters on one shared base model and batching their requests together, as in S-LoRA and Punica.
Training a student model to match a teacher's output distribution, not just the correct label (Hinton et al., 2015).
The teacher's full probability distribution over outputs, often softened with a temperature above 1 to expose how it ranks wrong answers.
KL(teacher || student). Mode covering: penalises the student for missing any place the teacher puts mass.
KL(student || teacher). Mode seeking: penalises the student for putting mass where the teacher doesn't. Used in on-policy distillation.
Training the student on complete outputs generated by the teacher (Kim and Rush, 2016). Works across tokenizers and through APIs.
The student generates text and the teacher scores each token, so the student learns to correct its own mistakes (Agarwal et al., 2024).
Sample many responses per prompt, keep those that pass a verifier or score highest with a reward model, and fine-tune on them.
Self-Taught Reasoner (Zelikman et al., 2022). Iteratively fine-tunes on the model's own reasoning traces that reach correct answers.
Generating new instruction data by prompting a model with seed examples, then filtering (Wang et al., 2023).
Progressive loss of distribution tails and quality when models are trained recursively on their own outputs (Shumailov et al., 2024). Mitigated by keeping real data in the mix.
A model made by averaging the weights of several fine-tunes of the same base (Wortsman et al., 2022).
The difference between fine-tuned and base weights. Task vectors can be added or subtracted to combine or remove skills (Ilharco et al., 2023).
A merging method that trims small weight changes, resolves sign conflicts, and averages only agreeing entries (Yadav et al., 2023).
